properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northern Martin County in east central Florida...
Eastern St. Lucie County in east central Florida...

* WHEN...Until 630 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 328 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain has
fallen on already saturated ground.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Port Saint Lucie, Walton, Fort Pierce, Stuart, White City, Saint
Lucie Nuclear Power Plant, Fort Pierce Inlet, Jensen Beach,
Indrio, Sewall's Point, Indian River Estates, Port Saint Lucie
River Park, Fort Pierce South, Saint Lucie West, Fort Pierce
North, Nettles Island, Saint Lucie Airport, Saint Lucie Village
and Tradition.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Tornado Warning issued October 11 at 3:29PM EDT until October 11 at 4:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
At 329 PM EDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a tornado
was located near Calico, or 10 miles southeast of Ayden, moving
northeast at 35 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed. Damage
to roofs, windows, and vehicles will occur.  Tree damage is
likely.

Locations impacted include...
Washington, Calico, Shelmerdine, Black Jack, Wilmar, Chocowinity,
Grimesland, and Gardnerville.
properties.instruction:
TAKE COVER NOW! Move to a basement or an interior room on the lowest
floor of a sturdy building. Avoid windows. If you are outdoors, in a
mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter
and protect yourself from flying debris.

If a tornado or other severe weather is spotted, report it to the
National Weather Service or your local nearest law enforcement agency
who will send your report. This act may save lives of others in the
path of dangerous weather.

Park. This will begin to produce flooding of portions of the lower
boardwalk. At 17.0 feet, The access road to the Sandy Run

National Park becomes flooded by Cedar Creek.

will then fall below flood stage late Thursday evening.
- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

roadway or around barricades. Turn around, don't drown.

through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Monday morning at 800 AM EDT.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 11 at 12:18PM MDT until October 11 at 3:15PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
FFWSLC

The National Weather Service in Salt Lake City has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Forsyth burn scar in...
Central Washington County in southwestern Utah...

* Until 315 PM MDT.

* At 1218 PM MDT, Emergency management reported heavy rain over the
Forsyth Burn Scar, and river gauges are rising rapidly along the
Santa Clara River. Between 1.25 and 2.25 inches of rain have
fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.
Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result in debris flow.
The debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other
loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding in and around the Forsyth Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Emergency management reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Forsyth Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Pine Valley.

This includes Utah Route 18 between mile markers 26 and 27.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and ditches
in the Forsyth Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated
across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in places. If
you encounter flood waters...climb to safety.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...western Coconino, northern Gila, far southern Navajo, and
Yavapai counties.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Flash flooding will be possible in creeks, normally dry
washes, swimming holes, and over recently burned areas. Raging
killer currents will be possible in side canyons and narrow slot
canyons. Low-water crossings may be flooded.

- Numerous showers and thunderstorms are expected to continue
across the area through tonight. With tropical moisture in place
from the remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel, periods of embedded
heavy rainfall will be possible this afternoon which could lead
to flash flooding. Additionally, the extended period of rain
could lead to elevated flow in creeks, normally dry washes, and
rivers.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 11 at 7:04AM SST by NWS Pago Pago  AS
properties.description:
ESFPPG

An active trough to the north is projected to drift southward and
move over the territory by midweek. This trough should remain
strong and active while over the territory, and may even intensify
with embedded low pressure centers. Widespread showers may be
heavy and persistent at times with the possibility of
thunderstorms. Widespread flash flooding may occur from this
rainfall, and landslides will be possible along steep mountainous
terrain. Impacts could begin as early as Wednesday and are
expected to persist through the weekend. While there is still
uncertainty in the exact magnitude and duration of rainfall, plan
now for wet conditions that could start as early as Wednesday and
persist through at least Sunday.

Keep up to date with the latest forecast information through our
internet page (www.weather.gov/ppg), local media, social media,
and our NOAA Radio broadcasts.

NWSheadline: Flash Flooding and landslide potential for Wednesday through Sunday

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 11 at 11:04AM MST until October 11 at 1:15PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
FFWPSR

The National Weather Service in Phoenix has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Sand Stone and Spring burn scar in...
Gila County in east central Arizona...
Maricopa County in south central Arizona...

* Until 115 PM MST.

* At 1104 AM MST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain over the Sand Stone and Spring
Burn Scars, as well as across portions of northeast Maricopa
County. Between 0.75 and 2 inches of rain have fallen. Flash
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly. Excessive
rainfall over the burn scar will result in debris flow. The debris
flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose
materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Sand Stone and Spring
Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Sand Stone and Spring Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Ballantine Trailhead, Round Valley, Sugarloaf Mountain, Sunflower,
Sycamore Creek, Saguaro Lake and Salt River Tubing Recreation Area.

This includes AZ Route 87 between mile markers 196 and 205.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and ditches
in the Sand Stone and Spring Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also
be anticipated across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away
in places. If you encounter flood waters...climb to safety.

Move away from recently burned areas. Life-threatening flooding of
creeks, roads and normally dry arroyos is likely. The heavy rains
will likely trigger rockslides, mudslides and debris flows in steep
terrain, especially in and around these areas.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.areaDesc: Carroll, VA; Pulaski, VA
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 11 at 1:25PM EDT until October 11 at 6:15PM EDT by NWS Blacksburg VA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Eastern Carroll County in southwestern Virginia...
South Central Pulaski County in southwestern Virginia...

* WHEN...Until 615 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying areas and along Big Reed
Island Creek. Some low-water crossings may become impassable as
flows along the creek are running high.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 120 PM EDT, minor flooding is occurring along Big Reed Island
Creek due to between 3 and 4 inches of rain that occurred between
Saturday morning and this morning. Water levels will remain high
through this afternoon, and will begin to recede by early
evening.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Island Creek, Burks Fork, Grassy Creek, Kings Run, Deepwater
Creek, Birds Branch and Johnson Creek.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Allisonia and Laurel Fork.
- For flooding safety information, please visit
http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

When it is safe to do so, please send your reports of flooding,
including mudslides or flooded roads, to the National Weather Service
by calling toll free at 1...8 6 6...2 1 5...4 3 2 4. Reports and
pictures can also be shared on the National Weather Service
Blacksburg Facebook page and on X.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 11 at 1:11PM EDT until October 11 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Wilmington NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents. Strong south to north longshore
current is also expected for east and southeast-facing beaches.

* WHERE...In North Carolina, Coastal Pender, Coastal New Hanover
and Coastal Brunswick Counties. In South Carolina, Coastal
Horry and Coastal Georgetown Counties.

* WHEN...Today.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Coconino, AZ; Gila, AZ; Yavapai, AZ
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 11 at 10:11AM MST until October 11 at 1:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Gila County in east central Arizona...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...
Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 100 PM MST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in creeks and normally dry washes is
imminent or occurring. Water flowing over roadways will create
slick roads and muddy unpaved roads.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1005 AM MST, trained weather spotters reported heavy rain in
the advisory area due to thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing
or expected to begin shortly. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have
fallen.
- This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Davenport Wash, Larry Creek, Corduroy Wash, West Clear Creek,
Clear Creek, Kinder Draw, Hardscrabble Creek, Dry Wash, Houston
Creek, Gap Creek, Pigeon Creek, South Prong Sycamore Creek, West
Webber Creek, North Fork Deadman Creek, Little Squaw Creek,
Little Ash Creek, Bull Run Creek, Horse Creek, Deadman Creek,
Cienega Creek, East Branch Squaw Creek, Dry Creek, Tangle Creek,
Silver Creek, Verde River, Cold Water Creek, Bishop Creek, Tank
Creek, Jacks Canyon, Indian Creek, Spring Wash, Little Sycamore
Creek, New River, Ash Spring Creek, Sycamore Creek, Fossil Creek,
Red Creek and Wet Bottom Creek. Additional rainfall amounts of
0.5 to 1.5 inches are expected over the area. This additional
rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Payson, Camp Verde, Pine, Strawberry, Mesa Del Caballo, Round
Valley, Verde Lakes, East Verde Estates, Deer Creek, Oxbow
Estates, Mountain View Estates, Beaver Valley Estates, Fort
McDonald, Ellison Creek Cascades, Whispering Pines, Washington
Park, Jakes Corner and Rye.
- This includes the following highways...
State Route 260 between mile markers 222 and 254. State Route 188
between mile markers 274 and 276. State Route 87 southbound
between mile markers 241 and 251. State Route 87 between mile
markers 230 and 295.

This includes the following recreation areas andcampgrounds...
Geronimo Boy Scout Camp, Rock Crossing Campground, Clints Well
Campground, Clear Creek Group Campgrounds, Houston Mesa
Campground, Kehl Springs Campground, Rumsey Park, Green Valley
Park and Shadow Rim Ranch.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Water Wheel Falls, Ellison Creek Cascades, All swimming holes and
waterfalls on Fossil Creek, Bull Pen Day Use Area, West Clear
Creek near the campground, Fossil Creek Dam "The Toilet Bowl" and
Indian Maiden Falls.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.areaDesc: Ashe, NC; Watauga, NC; Wilkes, NC
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 11 at 12:53PM EDT until October 11 at 4:00PM EDT by NWS Blacksburg VA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...South Central Ashe County in northwestern North Carolina...
Watauga County in northwestern North Carolina...
Southwestern Wilkes County in northwestern North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 400 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas. Strong
flows over low-water crossings will continue through late
afternoon, especially those along the Watauga River in western
Watauga County. While most rivers continue to recede this
afternoon, water remains over a few roadways, including Todd
Railroad Grade Road along the South Fork of the New River.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1250 PM EDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
rainfall has ended. Minor flooding persists within the advisory
area due to between 4.5 and 7.5 inches of rain that fell from
Saturday morning through this morning.  Area creeks and rivers
will continue to recede through the afternoon.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Fall Creek, Norris Fork, Flat Branch, Elk Creek, Mill Creek,
Dugger Creek, Little Dugger Creek, Laurel Fork, Dutch Creek, Meat
Camp Creek, Brushy Fork, Grassy Creek and Left Prong Stony Fork.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Boone, Blowing Rock, Deep Gap, Todd, Foscoe, Seven Devils and
Aho.
- For flooding safety information, please visit
http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

When it is safe to do so, please send your reports of flooding,
including mudslides or flooded roads, to the National Weather Service
by calling toll free at 1...8 6 6...2 1 5...4 3 2 4. Reports and
pictures can also be shared on the National Weather Service
Blacksburg Facebook page and on X.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 11 at 11:01AM EDT until October 11 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6
to 7 feet in the surf zone. For the Beach Hazards Statement,
dangerous rip currents and large breaking waves in the surf
zone.

* WHERE...Hatteras Island beaches, and Ocracoke Island beaches.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM EDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water. Dangerous shore
break can throw a swimmer or surfer head first into the bottom
causing neck and back injuries.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The most likely time for strong rip
currents to occur is a couple hours either side of low tide,
which will occur around 3 PM Sunday.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Life-threatening rip currents. If caught in a rip current, remain
calm. Swim in a direction following the shoreline. If tired,
float or tread water until out of the rip current. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

Shore break occurs when waves break directly on the beach. It is
extremely important to protect your head and neck whenever you
are in breaking waves by keeping your hands in front of you at
all times.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 11 at 7:19AM PDT until October 14 at 4:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.5 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bayshore locations along the San Pablo Bay.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM PDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. High tides will result in
flooding along coastal trails, cut off access to some low-
lying beaches and coastal areas, and bring water and waves
farther up the beach than typical. Dangerous conditions are
forecast along the shoreline. Hazards include sneaker waves,
strong rip currents, and large breaking waves.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high
tide is expected to be 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at
12:18 PM Sunday 10/11, 1.2 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at
12:46 PM Monday 10/12, 1.1 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at
1:14 PM Tuesday 10/13, and 0.9 ft above normal (6.7 ft MLLW)
at 1:46 PM Wednesday 10/14. These predictions include up to
1.2 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and
flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or
later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco
Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 11 at 10:09AM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Cypress Creek At SR 54 Worthington Gardens affecting Pasco County.

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Marion, Citrus and Levy
Counties.

.Due to recent heavy rainfall, water levels on Cypress Creek remain
elevated. With additional heavy rainfall forecast, water levels are
expected to continue rising, and could reach minor flood stage in the
next few days.

Elevated water levels continue on the Withlacoochee River at
Dunnellon due to a combination of excessive hydrilla growth along a
4.5 mile stretch of river between U.S. 41 and Lake Rousseau, and
recent heavy rainfall. Water levels are expected to hold steady
before slowly decreasing over the next several days. However, the
river is forecast to remain in flood stage.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 28.2 feet, Docks and boat ramps flood along the river
in Citrus and Marion counties.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:45 AM EDT Sunday the stage was 28.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 28.2 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:45 AM EDT Sunday was 28.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady at flood stage.
- Flood stage is 28.2 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.2
feet on 10/02/1979.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.areaDesc: Allegheny, PA; Beaver, PA; Butler, PA; Washington, PA; Westmoreland, PA
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 11 at 9:52AM EDT until October 11 at 4:30PM EDT by NWS Pittsburgh PA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Localized flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Allegheny County in southwestern Pennsylvania...
Central Washington County in southwestern Pennsylvania...
Western Westmoreland County in southwestern Pennsylvania...
Southwestern Butler County in west central Pennsylvania...
Central Beaver County in western Pennsylvania...

* WHEN...Until 430 PM EDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall. It
will take several hours for all the water from these storms to work
through local drainage systems in urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 951 AM EDT, fire rescue personnel have reported flooding
occuring over area roadways. Between 2 and 3 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Pittsburgh, Penn Hills, Mount Lebanon, Bethel Park, Ross
Township, McCandless Township, Monroeville, Cranberry, Moon
Township, McMurray, Greensburg, McKeesport, Franklin Park,
Jeannette, Aliquippa, Canonsburg, Monaca, Vandergrift, Apollo and
Gastonville.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.areaDesc: Wasatch Plateau/Book Cliffs; Eastern Juab/Millard Counties; Central Mountains; Sanpete Valley; Sevier Valley; Castle Country; San Rafael Swell; Southwest Utah; Lower Washington County; Zion National Park; Southern Mountains; Upper Sevier River Valleys; Bryce Canyon Country; South Central Utah; Capitol Reef National Park and Vicinity; Western Canyonlands; Glen Canyon Recreation Area/Lake Powell
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 11 at 6:42AM MDT until October 12 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Castle
Country, Central Mountains, Eastern Juab/Millard Counties, San
Rafael Swell, Sanpete Valley, Sevier Valley, Wasatch Plateau/Book
Cliffs, Bryce Canyon Country, Capitol Reef National Park and
Vicinity, Glen Canyon Recreation Area/Lake Powell, South Central
Utah, Southern Mountains, Upper Sevier River Valleys, Western
Canyonlands, Lower Washington County, Southwest Utah and Zion
National Park. This also includes recent burn scars such as
Forsyth, Cottonwood, Silver King, France Canyon, and Monroe Canyon.

* WHEN...Through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, dry washes, slot canyons, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations such as slickrock areas and recent burn
scars. Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may
occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Anomalously high moisture from the remnants of Tropical Storm
Rachel will continue to impact the region. While this is expected
to be a long duration rainfall event, scattered instances of
heavier rainfall rates are expected with stronger storms yielding
flash flooding concerns given saturated soils and prior burn
scars.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 11 at 6:42AM MDT until October 12 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Western
Millard and Juab Counties, Bear Lake and Bear River Valley, Cache
Valley/Utah Portion, Eastern Box Elder County, Great Salt Lake
Desert and Mountains, Northern Wasatch Front, Salt Lake Valley,
Tooele and Rush Valleys, Utah Valley, Wasatch Back, Wasatch
Mountains I-80 North, Wasatch Mountains South of I-80, Western
Uinta Basin and Western Uinta Mountains. This includes recent burn
scars such as Rocky Canyon.

* WHEN...Through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and recent burn scars. Flooding may occur in poor
drainage and urban areas. Extensive street flooding and flooding of
creeks and rivers are possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Moisture associated with the remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel
will continue to spread into northern Utah producing a prolonged
rainfall event. In particular, moisture interacting with a
frontal boundary across far northern Utah may yield locally
heavier rainfall totals compared to other locations. As a result,
areal flooding is possible across northern Utah.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 11 at 5:35AM MDT until October 12 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Pocatello ID
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.
Additional amounts of 0.75 to 1.5 inches are expected with some
places pushing 2 inches.

* WHERE...Portions of central, eastern, south central, and southeast
Idaho, including the following areas, in central Idaho, Sun Valley
Region and Wood River Foothills. In eastern Idaho, Beaverhead -
Lemhi Highlands, Big Hole Mountains, Centennial Mountains - Island
Park and Teton Valley. In south central Idaho, Eastern Magic Valley
and Shoshone/Lava Beds. In southeast Idaho, Arco/Mud Lake Desert,
Bear Lake Valley, Bear River Range, Blackfoot Mountains, Caribou
Range, Franklin/Eastern Oneida Region, Lower Snake River Plain,
Marsh and Arbon Highlands, Raft River Region, Southern Hills/Albion
Mountains and Upper Snake River Plain.

* WHEN...Through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A prolonged period of rainfall is expected across eastern Idaho
throughout the weekend which could lead to some flooding across
parts of the advised area. An upper low moving into the Pacific
Northwest will combine with tropical moisture from Tropical
Cyclone Rachel to usher in a cooler, wetter weather pattern
across eastern Idaho.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.description:

Carolina...

French Broad River Near at Old Fanning Bridge Rd, 3 W Fletcher
affecting Henderson and Buncombe Counties.

.Excessive runoff from a widespread 4 to 5 inch storm total rainfall
will maintain flooding along the French Broad River.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...French Broad River near at Old Fanning Bridge Rd, 3 W
Fletcher.

* WHEN...Until Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, Action Stage continues.  Glenn Bridge Park
river access is experiencing minor flooding.  Westfeldt Park is
experiencing scattered flooding.  French Broad River floodwaters
are causing isolated to widely scattered farmland flooding.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:45 AM EDT Sunday the stage was 11.2 feet and rising.
- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of around
12.0 feet just after midnight tonight.
- Action stage is 10.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 13.0 feet.

Coastal Areas, San Diego County Deserts, San Diego County

of moderate to heavy rain to all of San Diego County, Riverside
County mountains and deserts, and San Bernardino County mountains
and deserts through late this afternoon. Maximum hourly rainfall
rates of 0.50 to 0.60 inches per hour are possible for San Diego

inch per hour rates are possible across area mountains. Heaviest
rainfall is most likely through early this afternoon. Rainfall
will taper off from south to north today. Lingering lighter
showers are expected to continue into Monday.

properties.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued October 11 at 3:53AM PDT until October 11 at 3:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning through Sunday afternoon,
significant coastal flooding and beach erosion is likely. For
the Beach Hazards Statement from Sunday morning until Sunday
evening, surf of 5 to 7 feet with local sets up to 9 feet. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory from Sunday afternoon until Tuesday
afternoon, minor coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 3 PM PDT Sunday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, from Sunday morning through
Sunday evening. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 PM
Sunday to 2 PM PDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads and beach boardwalks may be closed
due to high water. Low-lying property including homes,
businesses, and some critical infrastructure may flood during
morning high tides. Beach erosion. Elevated surf will lead to
a high risk of rip currents and dangerous swimming conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Greatest impacts on this morning from Post-Tropical
Cyclone Rachel with a combination of increased swell, onshore
winds, and high tides locally over 7.5 feet. High tides lower
each day into the middle of the week.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.

* WHERE...The beaches of Douglas, Coos, and Curry counties.

* WHEN...From 5 AM PDT early this morning through Monday
afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Sneaker waves can run up significantly farther on
beaches than normal, including over rocks and jetties. These

them into the ocean. The waves can also move logs or other
objects which could crush or trap anyone caught underneath.

* View the hazard area in detail at
https://www.wrh.noaa.gov/map/?wfo=mfr

remain out of the water to avoid hazardous conditions.

are possible.

* WHERE...Portions of eastern, northeast, and south central Nevada,
including the following areas, in eastern Nevada, White Pine. In
northeast Nevada, the Ruby Mountains and East Humboldt Range in
Elko, South Central Elko and Southeastern Elko. In south central
Nevada, Northeastern Nye and Northwestern Nye.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams,
and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. In addition, flash
flooding is possible over recently burned areas like the former
Ward Fire, Kearny Fire, Oxley Fire, Secret Pass Fire, Starr Valley
Fire, Jones Fire, and Egberts Fire. Other burn scar locations in
the watch area could also be affected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Deep moisture from decaying Hurricane Rachel is expected to move
northward, crossing into portions of east-central and eastern
Nevada late tonight through roughly Monday. This significant
moisture will interact with upper level low pressure to bring
widespread showers with isolated thunderstorms to the watch area.
Moderate to locally heavy rain will cause excessive runoff and
may result in rock, mud, and debris flows in and near former fire
burned areas, steep terrain, and poorly drained urban areas.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 11 at 2:20AM EDT until October 11 at 6:00PM EDT by NWS Marquette MI
properties.description:
* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 002 Ontonagon and Fire
Weather Zone 009 Gogebic.

* TIMING...Until 6 PM EDT /5 PM CDT/ this evening.

* WINDS...Southwest 5 to 15 mph with gusts up to 25 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 32 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures and
exceptionally dry fuels will create dangerous wildland fire
conditions. Campfires, outdoor grills, smoking materials,
fireworks, chain saws, and all-terrain vehicles all have the
potential to throw a spark and ignite a dangerous and destructive
fire.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 11 at 2:04AM EDT until October 13 at 8:00AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in South
Carolina...North Carolina...

(English) Broad River Near at Shelby Hwy (SC 18), 4 W Blacksburg
affecting Cherokee and Cleveland Counties.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...(English) Broad River near at Shelby Hwy (SC 18), 4 W
Blacksburg.

* WHEN...Until Tuesday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Action Stage Flooding continues.  The Broad
River may be approaching River Rd. and Little Hope Rd. near US 29.
Adjacent farmland and low-lying area flooding is continuing.

* At 16.0 feet, Minor Flood Stage.  The Broad River may be flooding
River Rd. and Little Hope Rd. near US 29.  Farmland flooding is
continuing adjacent to the river.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:45 AM EDT Sunday the stage was 6.3 feet and rising steadily.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 15.0 feet
later this evening.
- Action/Advisory Stage is 8.0 feet.
- Minor Flood Stage is 16.0 feet.
properties.instruction:
If you encounter a flooded roadway, turn around and find an
alternative route.

If you are in the Advisory area, remain alert to possible flooding or
the possibility of the Advisory being upgraded to a Warning.

For detailed information including observed and forecast stages,
flood impacts, flood history, FEMA Flood Hazard Layers, and more,
please visit: https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/GSP

The next statement should be issued this afternoon before 215 PM EDT.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Del Norte; Northern Coastal Humboldt; Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 10 at 10:13PM PDT until October 12 at 5:00PM PDT by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...A very long period westerly swell will increase the
threat of sneaker waves.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Northern Coastal Humboldt,
Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...From 4 AM PDT Sunday through Monday afternoon. .

* IMPACTS...Large, unexpected waves can sweep across the beach
without warning, sweeping people into the sea from rocks,
jetties, and beaches. These sneaker waves can also move large
objects such as logs, crushing anyone caught underneath.
properties.instruction:
Don't be fooled by an ocean that looks calm.  There can be
30 minutes of small waves before a sneaker wave strikes.  Avoid
rocks and jetties. Avoid steep beaches.  Stay much farther back
from the water and never turn your back on the ocean.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...West central and southwest Florida.

* WHEN...For the Rip Current Risk, through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 10 at 1:51PM PDT until October 13 at 2:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...DAMAGING sea-water coastal flooding is likely through
Sunday, especially near the Sunday morning high tide where
anticipated tide levels are expected to be around 8 feet. The
most likely areas for DAMAGING coastal flooding on Sunday
morning will be vulnerable southeast facing beaches, such as
Avalon and Pebbly Beach. For all other beaches and harbors,
minor to moderate coastal flooding is expected. The most
DAMAGING and WIDESPREAD coastal flooding risk along southeast
beaches will likely be with the Sunday morning high tide due to
the expected combination of very high level tide levels
approaching 8 feet (including additive effect of low barometric
pressure, high surf of 5 to 8 feet, and light to moderate
rainfall.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 3 PM PDT Sunday.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 PM Sunday to 2 PM PDT
Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Sea-water flooding of beach and harbor roads, parking
lots, and walkways is likely, especially around the time of high
tide. Isolated damage is likely across southeast facing beaches
near Sunday mornings high tide. Significant beach erosion is
expected. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides of around 8 feet are expected on
Sunday morning, returning to around 7.5 feet for Monday and
Tuesday mornings. Large secondary high tides are also expected
each evening.
properties.instruction:
Stay off of beaches and coastal walkways, roads, and structures.
Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

properties.areaDesc: Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 10 at 1:51PM PDT until October 11 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...DAMAGING sea-water coastal flooding is likely through
Sunday, especially near the Sunday morning high tide where
anticipated tide levels are expected to be around 8 feet. The
most likely areas for DAMAGING coastal flooding on Sunday
morning will be vulnerable south-facing beaches due to the
expected combination of very high level tide levels around 8
feet (including additive effect of low barometric pressure and
onshore winds gusting to 15 to 25 mph), high surf of 5 to 8
feet, and light to moderate rainfall. For all other beaches,
minor to moderate coastal flooding is expected near times of
high tide. From Sunday night through Tuesday, there will be the
continued threat of at least minor to moderate coastal flooding
and elevated surf across Los Angeles county beaches, especially
south facing shores. Dangerous rip currents are likely.

* WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 3 PM PDT Sunday.
For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM to 10 PM PDT Sunday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 PM Sunday to 2 PM PDT
Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...For vulnerable south-facing beaches (such as Alamitos
Peninsula and Naples in Long Beach as well as Malibu),
SIGNIFICANT sea- water flooding will likely DAMAGE coastal
structures and beach roadways around the time of high tide,
especially the Sunday morning high tide. In addition,
significant ponding of water on low-lying beach roadways could
make driving difficult. THERE IS GROWING CONFIDENCE THAT THE
EXPECTED COASTAL FLOODING IMPACTS ON SUNDAY MORNING FOR
VULNERABLE SOUTH FACING BEACHES OF LA COUNTY COULD BE THE MOST
SIGNIFICANT WE HAVE SEEN SO FAR THIS SEASON, INCLUDING THOSE
SEEN WITH MARIE. For all other beaches and harbors, shallow with
minor to moderate sea- water flooding will likely impact
beaches and walkways, especially with the Sunday morning high
tide which could cause local damage to most vulnerable locations
such as Venice. For all beach areas, significant erosion is
expected. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning.
Dangerous and life- threatening rip currents can pull swimmers
and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury,
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near
shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides of around 8 feet are expected on
Sunday morning (nearly 2 feet above astronomical high tide of
6.1 feet), returning to around 7.5 feet for Monday and Tuesday
mornings. The projected high tides of around 8 feet for Sunday
morning would approach or exceed recent record tide levels for
LA county. Large secondary high tides are also expected each
evening.
properties.instruction:
Follow directions of emergency officials.
Stay off of beaches and coastal walkways, roads, and structures.
Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 10 at 1:51PM PDT until October 12 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, Minor tidal overflow
flooding and strong rip currents are expected. For the Coastal
Flood Advisory, minor to moderate coastal flooding can be
expected near times of high tide, especially with the Sunday
morning high tide. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 8 to 12 feet is expected with dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through late tonight.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 6 AM Sunday to 10 PM PDT
Monday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM Sunday to 10 PM
PDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Minor to moderate flooding of sea water is likely
around high tide at beach and harbor areas that is uncommon with
normal tidal ranges. Low lying areas will be most susceptible,
including Oceano. Enhanced beach erosion is likely. The risk for
significant damage is very low. There is an increased risk of
ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out
to sea. Waves can wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats nearshore. Large secondary high tides are also
expected each evening.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides are expected to peak around 7.5
feet on Sunday morning, then around 7 feet on Monday morning.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 PM PDT Tuesday.
For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM to 10 PM PDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Sea-water flooding of beach and harbor roads, parking
lots, and walkways is likely, especially around the time of high
tide. Isolated damage is possible during the Sunday morning high
tide which is expected to peak around 8 feet. The most
vulnerable locations to coastal flooding will be low-lying areas
from Ventura to LA county line. Localized pockets of Highway 1
between Point Mugu and LA county line could see significant surf
spray and some sea-water on the roadway. Significant beach
erosion is expected. There is an increased risk for ocean
drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea.
Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches
and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides approaching 8 feet will be
likely on Sunday morning (nearly 2 feet above astronomical high
tide of 6.1 feet), returning to around 7.5 feet for Monday and
Tuesday mornings. Large secondary high tides are also expected
each evening.

properties.areaDesc: Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 10 at 1:51PM PDT until October 13 at 2:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...DAMAGING sea-water coastal flooding is likely through
Sunday, especially near the Sunday morning high tide where
anticipated tide levels are expected to be around 8 feet. The
most likely areas for DAMAGING coastal flooding on Sunday
morning will be vulnerable south-facing beaches due to the
expected combination of very high level tide levels around 8
feet (including additive effect of low barometric pressure and
onshore winds gusting to 15 to 25 mph), high surf of 5 to 8
feet, and light to moderate rainfall. For all other beaches,
minor to moderate coastal flooding is expected near times of
high tide. From Sunday night through Tuesday, there will be the
continued threat of at least minor to moderate coastal flooding
and elevated surf across Los Angeles county beaches, especially
south facing shores. Dangerous rip currents are likely.

* WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 3 PM PDT Sunday.
For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM to 10 PM PDT Sunday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 PM Sunday to 2 PM PDT
Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...For vulnerable south-facing beaches (such as Alamitos
Peninsula and Naples in Long Beach as well as Malibu),
SIGNIFICANT sea- water flooding will likely DAMAGE coastal
structures and beach roadways around the time of high tide,
especially the Sunday morning high tide. In addition,
significant ponding of water on low-lying beach roadways could
make driving difficult. THERE IS GROWING CONFIDENCE THAT THE
EXPECTED COASTAL FLOODING IMPACTS ON SUNDAY MORNING FOR
VULNERABLE SOUTH FACING BEACHES OF LA COUNTY COULD BE THE MOST
SIGNIFICANT WE HAVE SEEN SO FAR THIS SEASON, INCLUDING THOSE
SEEN WITH MARIE. For all other beaches and harbors, shallow with
minor to moderate sea- water flooding will likely impact
beaches and walkways, especially with the Sunday morning high
tide which could cause local damage to most vulnerable locations
such as Venice. For all beach areas, significant erosion is
expected. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning.
Dangerous and life- threatening rip currents can pull swimmers
and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury,
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near
shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides of around 8 feet are expected on
Sunday morning (nearly 2 feet above astronomical high tide of
6.1 feet), returning to around 7.5 feet for Monday and Tuesday
mornings. The projected high tides of around 8 feet for Sunday
morning would approach or exceed recent record tide levels for
LA county. Large secondary high tides are also expected each
evening.
properties.instruction:
Follow directions of emergency officials.
Stay off of beaches and coastal walkways, roads, and structures.
Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.areaDesc: Imperial County Southwest; Imperial County Southeast; Imperial County West; Imperial Valley
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued October 10 at 9:31AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...The Imperial County APCD has issued an air quality alert
due to harmful levels of particle pollution from windblown dust.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...the Imperial Valley. Levels of particle pollution can vary
by time and location depending on emissions and local weather
conditions.

* WHEN...Sunday, October 11, 2026 from 12:00 AM until 10:00 PM.

* IMPACTS... Particle pollution can get deep into the lungs and
cause serious health problems such as asthma attacks, heart and lung
disease symptoms, and increased risk of lung infections. Everyone
can be affected, but sensitive groups such as people with lung or
heart disease, older adults, people who are pregnant, children, and
those who spend a lot of time outdoors are at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:

* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are "Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups" (orange), sensitive groups as specified
above should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Unhealthy" (red), everyone may experience health
impacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.
* When AQI is "Very Unhealthy" (purple), sensitive groups should
avoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should
avoid extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Hazardous" (maroon), everyone should avoid all
outdoor physical activity.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

To help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:

* Keep windows and doors closed
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, grilling, and gasoline-powered lawn and garden
equipment

To help minimize outdoor particle pollution levels:

* Carpool, telecommute, reduce trips, or take public
transportation
* Slow down if driving on dirt roads
* Stabilize loose soils
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 9 at 10:53AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
ESFGJT

A strong low pressure system off the Pacific Coast will begin to draw
in tropical moisture associated with Topical Storm Rachel this
weekend. This strong southerly fetch will draw anomalously high
moisture content across the Desert Southwest and into eastern Utah
and western Colorado. The chance for widespread precipitation
increases Saturday evening into Sunday. Total precipitation forecasts
range from 1 to 3 inches across high terrain, with highest amounts
favoring the Uintas, Tavaputs and the Southwest San Juan mountains.

Embedded thunderstorms are also possible Sunday afternoon, increasing
the threat for flash flooding across vulnerable terrain. While
confidence in location and rainfall rates remain low at this time,
the potential for rapidly rising rivers, streams, normally dry
arroyos and slot canyons are possible Sunday through Monday.

Please follow the evolving forecast, especially if your plans
including recreating or commuting across eastern Utah and western
Colorado Sunday onward. Also, keep in mind weather potential above
your location and upstream, particularly for those who reside below
sensitive terrain like recent burn scars.
